title: LearnPyTorch · Tensor Lab
summary: Build tensor intuition by changing code and inspecting values. Three guided lessons cover axis order, broadcasting, and batched matrix multiplication.
detail: 3 interactive lessons · Browser-only tensor simulator · Python export
intro: Each tile is a value, each axis gives it a position. Predict what an operation will do, run it, then inspect the result. The starter programs contain deliberate mistakes: a program can run and still arrange the data incorrectly.
workflow: Choose a lesson, edit the code, and select Run. Compare your result with the target and select an intermediate step to inspect it. Hints progress from an idea to a solution. A lesson passes only when shapes and values match on the visible example and three fresh inputs.
privacy: Progress stays in this browser when storage is available. Code runs locally in a bounded simulator; it is not sent to a server. Share copies your code into a URL. Python export creates a file you can run in an environment with PyTorch installed.
scope: This is a PyTorch-style simulator, not a full Python runtime. It supports numeric tensors of rank 0–4 with up to 4096 elements and positive dimensions. The canvas shows up to 8 × 8 cells per slice. Indexing, loops, autograd, devices, dtypes, empty tensors, and in-place changes are outside this release. Noncontiguous reshape conservatively copies here; real PyTorch can sometimes return a view. Export uses floating-point tensors explicitly.
api: Reorder axes while preserving which element belongs where.
Swap two axes; negative axes count from the end.
Regroup the logical element sequence; one -1 can infer a dimension.
Insert or remove a size-one axis.
Reduce an axis; keepdim=True retains its position for broadcasting.
Elementwise arithmetic with broadcasting, or matrix multiplication with @.
Create a tensor from nested lists or the numbers 0 through n−1.
Create tensors filled with ones or zeros.
independent: Independent learning project, inspired by Learn Git Branching; not affiliated with PyTorch.

notes.permute: Axes are reordered while values keep their identity. The underlying storage is shared, not rearranged.
notes.reshape: The logical element sequence is regrouped. Contiguous inputs share storage; this simulator copies noncontiguous inputs.
notes.singleton: Size-one axes were inserted or removed. Storage is shared.
notes.reduction: Values are reduced along the selected axis. keepdim=True leaves a size-one axis for broadcasting.
notes.matmul: The inner matrix axes contract. Each output cell is a dot product; leading batch axes broadcast.
notes.arithmetic: Axes align from the right. Size-one axes reuse input values; the output gets new storage.
notes.new: A new tensor with its own storage.

errors.broadcast: Cannot broadcast these shapes. Align axes from the right: dimensions must match or one must be 1. Try keepdim=True or unsqueeze().
errors.matmul: Matrix multiplication needs matching inner dimensions and rank 2–4 tensors. Try transpose(-2, -1) on the second operand.
errors.reshape: reshape must preserve the number of elements. Use positive integer dimensions and at most one -1.
errors.axis: The axes are invalid. Use an in-range integer; permute must include every axis exactly once.
errors.limit: Keep code under 6000 characters, use at most 100 operations, and keep tensors within rank 4 and 4096 elements.
errors.finite: Values must be finite numbers and nested rows must have equal lengths. Check division by zero.
errors.syntax: This expression is not supported or is incomplete. Check the API guide, variable names, brackets, and arguments. Use one assignment per line.

lessons.title: A change of perspective
lessons.intro: An image is more than a list of numbers. Move its axes without losing the relationship between pixels and channels.
lessons.goal: Turn x from [height, width, channel] into y with [channel, height, width]. Keep every pixel in the right place.
lessons.concept: reshape changes how a sequence is grouped. permute changes which axis comes first. Equal shapes do not guarantee equal values.
lessons.starter:
# x: [height, width, channel] = [2, 3, 2]
# Move channels to the first axis.
y = x.reshape(2, 2, 3)
hints: The original axes are 0 = height, 1 = width, 2 = channel.
The new order is old axis 2, then old axis 0, then old axis 1.
Try y = x.permute(2, 0, 1). Inspect the values, not just the shape.
lessons.takeaway: You preserved which pixel each value belongs to. permute reorders axes and shares storage; reshape alone cannot perform this swap.
lessons.transfer: Convert [batch, height, width, channel] into [batch, channel, height, width]. Which axis stays in place?

lessons.title: Give every row its space
lessons.intro: Subtract each row’s average. The shape of the means determines where their values are reused.
lessons.goal: Create y by subtracting each row’s mean from that same row of x. Every output row should have mean zero.
lessons.concept: Broadcasting aligns axes from the right. Dimensions must match or one must be 1. keepdim=True retains the reduced axis with size 1.
lessons.starter:
# x has shape [3, 3]
# This runs, but does it center each row?
means = x.mean(dim=1)
y = x - means
hints: For a square input, [3] aligns with columns. Code can run while subtracting the wrong values.
You need one mean per row with shape [3, 1]. Retain axis 1 when reducing.
Use means = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True), then y = x - means.
lessons.takeaway: Each row reuses its own mean. This solution also works on rectangular inputs, where the original code fails.
lessons.transfer: For x [batch, time, features], subtract the mean over time for each batch and feature. Which dim should you reduce?

lessons.title: Keep the batch together
lessons.intro: Compare every query to every key, independently for each batch item. Each batch has its own matrix multiplication.
lessons.goal: Produce y [batch, query, key]. Each score must be the dot product of a query and a key from the same batch.
lessons.concept: With @, the last two axes are matrix axes and earlier axes are batch axes. Swap the key and feature axes of k so feature dimensions contract.
lessons.starter:
# q: [batch, query, feature] = [2, 2, 3]
# k: [batch, key, feature] = [2, 4, 3]
y = q @ k
hints: The feature axes both have size 3. They must be q’s last axis and k’s second-last axis.
Change k from [2, 4, 3] to [2, 3, 4], keeping the batch axis in place.
lessons.takeaway: Each batch contains a query-by-key score matrix. Feature axes contract while batches stay independent—the shape pattern behind attention scores.
lessons.transfer: For q [B, H, Q, D] and k [B, H, K, D], predict the shape of q @ k.transpose(-2, -1).

sandbox.title: Follow your curiosity
sandbox.intro: Create a tensor, change its shape, and follow each operation. Reset restores the starting experiment.
sandbox.goal: Explore freely. Try a different dim, add keepdim=True, or transpose before reshaping.
sandbox.concept: Select a step to inspect values, axes, and storage. The API guide lists the supported expressions.
sandbox.starter:
x = torch.arange(12).reshape(3, 4)
means = x.mean(dim=1, keepdim=True)
y = x - means
